To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the InsP 3 receptor (InsP 3 R) and chromogranin form a functional unit that amplifies Ca 2+ release from intracellular stores.
the interaction of the InsP3 receptor with chromogranins in the lumen enhances the sensitivity of the receptor to InsP3.

the inositol-1,4, 5-trisphospate receptor (InsP(3)R), which is a Ca(2+) release channel in the endoplasmatic reticulum (the intracellular Ca(2+) storage organelle), is functionally coupled to chromogranin (a Ca(2+) binding protein).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional coupling of the InsP3 receptor with its endogenous ligand, chromogranin.
the functional coupling of chromogranins with InsP3 R. Chromogranin A (CgA) and chromogranin B (CgB) are high capacity, but low affinity calcium storage proteins that bind the InsP3 receptor (IP3R).
the functional role of the InsP3 receptor/chromogranins in the regulation of intracellular Ca2+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chromogranins are important for the regulation of Ca2+ signaling and that they are an essential component of the InsP3 receptor complex.
chromogranins are essential components of a functional complex that amplifies InsP3 R activity and thereby Ca2+ signaling.
the interaction between chromogranin and InsP3 R is an important mechanism for amplifying Ca2+ release in the ER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chromogranins are not simply storage proteins, but also play important roles in Ca2+-signaling.
chromogranins are essential for the proper function of the InsP3 receptor.
chromogranins are essential for the amplification of Ca2+ signaling by InsP3R type 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the InsP(3)R/chromograin complex is an important regulator of Ca(2+) release from the ER.
chromogranins are not only important regulators of Ca2+ signaling in neuroendocrine cells but that they are also involved in the modulation of Ca2+ signals in other cell types.
chromogranins are important regulators of Ca2+ release.
